# Evaluating ocean forecasting systems

OceanBench scores ocean forecasts against observations, the 2024 [GLORYS reanalysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030) and the 2024 [GLO12 analysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_ANALYSISFORECAST_PHY_001_024).
No single metric tells the whole story, so the scores cover several variables and references.

Submit a model or contribute on [GitHub](https://github.com/mercator-ocean/oceanbench/).
1 degree track method: see the [docs](https://oceanbench.readthedocs.io/en/latest/one-degree-track.html).
Explore the fields in the [Viewer](viewer.qmd).

```{python}
#| output: asis

# The region descriptions and bounds the region globe draws are static site metadata, not
# score data, so they are stamped into the page rather than fetched.
import json

from helpers.published_regions import published_region_ids, published_region_metadata

region_metadata = {region_id: published_region_metadata(region_id) for region_id in published_region_ids()}
print(f"<script>window.OCEANBENCH_REGION_METADATA = {json.dumps(region_metadata)};</script>")
```

::: {#all-scores}

<p id="scores-status" class="scores-status">Loading the published scores summary.</p>

## Comparison to observations

RMSE against observations (Class IV: altimetry SSH, in-situ T/S, drifter currents). Colors: % difference to the selected baseline.

<div id="observations-scores"></div>

## Comparison to reanalysis

RMSE against the 2024 [GLORYS reanalysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_PHY_001_030). The ML models are trained on GLORYS, so it is not a neutral reference for them.

<div id="reanalysis-scores"></div>

## Comparison to analysis

RMSE against the 2024 [GLO12 analysis](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/product/GLOBAL_ANALYSISFORECAST_PHY_001_024).
Caution at short leads: models started from the GLO12 nowcast begin near this analysis, so early scores flatter them.

<div id="analysis-scores"></div>
